In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proteome of S. myxoccoides and C. hutchisonii growing on crystalline celluose and pectine, respectively, is highly redundant, with a large number of hypothetical proteins being expressed.
the cellulolytic mechanisms used by C. hutchisonii and S. Myxococcoidies are highly redundant, but they are not cellulosomal.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have identified the proteome setup used by two soil Bacteroides species for cellulose degradation, and we have shown that these two proteomes represent a highly redundant set of putative cellulases.
the proteome of the soil bacterium Cytophaga (Sporocytophaga) hutchinsonii during cellulose degradation is dominated by enzymes of the GH5, GH8, GH9, and GH12 families.
the two cellulose-degrading Bacteroidetes C. hutchinsoii and S. Myxococcoidis have evolved a highly specific mode of cellulose degradation, which does not conform to current models.
The main takeaway from our work is that

we have identified a large number of putative cellulases that have never been studied before and that these enzymes might have an important role in the cellulolytic machinery used by the two Bacteroidetes bacteria.
the two Bacteroidetes cellulolytic bacteria have highly idiosyncratically adapted to their substrate.
the cellulose-degrading mechanisms used by the two soil Bacteroidete species are not well described by the current models for cellulolytic bacteria.
